title: Subword enumeration up to stack-sorting equivalence
summary: Defant and Kravitz introduced generalizations of West's stack-sorting map $s$ from permutations to finite words. This raises questions as to how such generalizations could be applied in the field of combinatorics on words. The Defant-Kravitz generalizations of $s$ depend on how repeated occurrences of the same character within a word may be repositioned, according to their $\textsf{tortoise}$ and $\textsf{hare}$ operations.
